core_struggle: Facing a returning tumour, she is not afraid of dying itself but is afraid of the pain and of becoming a burden to her children.
mirror: You are not afraid of dying exactly. You are afraid of the pain and of what it will cost your children.

queries.hook: The fear of pain and of becoming a burden to your children, not the fear of dying itself. I'm afraid of death.
queries.diagnose: Fear grows from imagining the future and from forgetting that what is real in us cannot be lost; worry multiplies what has not happened.
queries.steady: What is real in you cannot be lost, and what is lost was never you.
queries.act: Remember what is real in you and cannot be lost, and let your children hold what they must hold.
queries.story: A mother who faced her own end, afraid of the pain and of her children's grief, who found that what she was could not be taken.

weeks: The one who cannot be lost
emotion: afraid of burdening and of pain
bridge: The fear is not of the end but of what it costs your children, and the texts ask what is real in you that cannot be lost.
week_thesis: From the fear of pain and burden to the recognition that what is real in you cannot be lost, and the courage to let your children carry what they must.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the fear of pain and of becoming a burden, named without judgement.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that fear grows from imagining what will happen, and from forgetting what is real in you.
week_beats.steady: You hold that what is real in you cannot be lost, and what is lost was never you.
week_beats.act: You try remembering what is real in you and letting your children hold what they must.
week_beats.story: A mother who faced her own end, afraid of the pain and of her children's grief, shows you what could not be taken.

insight: You are not afraid of dying itself, but of the pain and of becoming a burden. What is real in you cannot be lost, and that is what the texts speak of.
details: tumour has returned and doctor has said so
